clue.text: Grouping Olympic finalists in Derby, for example

parts.note: a grouping or category is a class

indicators.note: finalists here are the final letters of the word Olympic, the closing pair

explanation.surface: Sports fans sort the Olympic finalists who will run in the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympic finalists' are its last two letters, IC. The Derby is a famous English flat horse race at Epsom, one of the five Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the five Classic races of British flat racing, so it is an example of that kind of race.

clue.text: Sulphur not present in make-up of heavenly body

indicators.note: not present in means the sulphur letter is removed from the make-up word

parts.note: make-up is cosmetic, applied for appearance
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur is absent from the make-up of a celestial body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like 'composition' but means face paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a comet, a heavenly body with a tail.

clue.text: Current song outpouring

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
an outpouring is a flow

explanation.surface: A popular song pours out emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'up to date', but means a stream of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airflow is a current of air moving over a surface.

clue.text: Big Kitty overturned this sailing-ship

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the pools, the football pools, are a big betting kitty

explanation.surface: A huge cat capsized this sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Kitty' is a big pot of money: the football pools, a British betting game, turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: This mini-banger is sometimes stuck

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a sausage; a little one is often served on a cocktail stick, while a mini firework might fail to go off

explanation.definitionFit: A small thin sausage, often speared on a cocktail stick at parties.

clue.text: Modern music pitch can make lighter work

parts.note: rock is a style of modern popular music
pitch is a black sticky substance, tar

explanation.surface: A modern music venue's pitch promises to make the work feel lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock tar is an old name for petroleum, the fuel that makes a lighter work; 'lighter' looks like 'less heavy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock tar is crude petroleum, a fuel from which lighter fluid is refined.

clue.text: Corroded game-pen

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A rusted pen used for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union, a ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is corroded has rust on it.

clue.text: X-ray" seen over a door?

parts.note: an X is a cross
a ray of light is a beam

explanation.surface: An X-ray picture shows something above a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'X-ray' into its two halves: X and ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A transverse beam such as a lintel sits horizontally above a doorway.

clue.text: Ploughing that goes on for years?

definitions.text: Ploughing that goes on for years?

parts.words: Ploughing that goes on for years?
parts.note: a playful split: turning soil that lasts until old age

explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing land for crops is tilling, and its noun is this word.

clue.text: Carrots can be blue in Australia!

explanation.definitionFit: Carrots is a nickname for someone with ginger hair, whom Australians jokingly call Bluey.

clue.text: Italian inventor who introduced polo, say, to Northern Ireland

indicators.note: one piece is brought up to and set before the other, joining them
one piece is brought up to and set before the other, joining them

parts.note: Marco Polo is an example of someone surnamed Polo

explanation.surface: An Italian inventor brought the game of polo to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polo' looks like the sport, but the 'say' points to Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian pioneer of radio, a famous inventor.

clue.text: Saint's head hooded and lowered

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
a head that is hooded has a cowl over it, so it is cowled

explanation.surface: A monk saint bowed his hooded head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowered' here is not 'brought down' but 'loured', an old spelling meaning to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour (also spelt lower) is to frown darkly, which is what one did who scowled.

clue.text: Calling people to produce polythene?

indicators.note: the letters of polythene are worked over to produce a new word

explanation.surface: A firm phones round to find people who can manufacture polythene.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of POLYTHENE, signalled by 'to produce', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephony is the business of making phone calls, of ringing people up.

clue.text: Post wager?

explanation.definitionFit: A pointed wooden post driven into the ground, and also money put on a bet.

clue.text: Jerseys, say, required in yachting-centre

indicators.note: say tells the solver the word for the cattle is spoken, giving a similar sound

parts.note: Jerseys are a breed of dairy cattle, so they are cows

explanation.surface: Sailors are told sweaters are needed at the yachting town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerseys' looks like knitted pullovers but means the Channel Island cattle. Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, is home to Cowes Week regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes on the Isle of Wight is Britain's best-known sailing town, hosting the Cowes Week regatta.

clue.text: Record of golfers (scratch, with proof of membership)

parts.note: to scratch a mark into something is to score it
a membership card proves you belong

explanation.surface: Club records note scratch golfers and their membership details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratch' looks like the golf term for a zero handicap, but means to score a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers note their strokes per hole on a card that records the round.

clue.text: Stop paper coming out before hospital closure

indicators.note: paper coming out is the word broken open and set in a new order

parts.note: a closure is an end

explanation.surface: A newspaper is halted just before a hospital is shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' is a verb here, to arrest; 'closure' supplies the end, and 'coming out' is the anagram signal for the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend a suspect is to arrest them, to stop them in their tracks.

clue.text: Ah! no one MEP can produce marvels

indicators.note: can produce means these letters are reworked into a new word

parts.note: no one means none

explanation.surface: A gasp: not a single Euro-MP can perform wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one' gives NONE, which goes into the mix with AH and MEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Marvels are remarkable occurrences, extraordinary things.

clue.text: Hot cola mixed in church-then sold in bars

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters between the two church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: hot cola that is mixed has its letters stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Hot cola is mixed in church, then sold at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' means slabs of confectionery, not pubs; the church is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery that comes in slabs is sold in bars, the usual form of the sweet made from cocoa.

clue.text: Starting cricket, play so whimsically-with the air of a West Indian

definitions.text: the air of a West Indian

indicators.note: starting means taking only the opening letter of cricket
whimsically means the letters of play so are capriciously rearranged

explanation.surface: Caribbean cricketers start a game playing in a carefree way.
explanation.walkthrough: C (start of cricket) plus ALYPSO, a rearrangement of PLAY SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of Caribbean song, especially from Trinidad.

clue.text: Keep an eye on commentator who is one run short!

indicators.note: short means one letter, run, is missing from the commentator

parts.note: an observer is a commentator
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator watches a batsman one run short of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: OBSERVER loses one R.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch something carefully.

clue.text: Charm of river backing up engulfs soldier

indicators.note: engulfs means the river surrounds the soldier
backing up means the river's name is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The beauty of a river flooding back to swallow a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river through Cambridge; 'backing up' turns it round and 'engulfs' wraps it around the American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm and magic are both spells or enchantment.

clue.text: Girl's first to refuse glamour

indicators.note: first means just the girl's opening letter

parts.note: refuse as a noun is rubbish, litter

explanation.surface: A girl is the first to turn down showbiz glamour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like the verb 'decline' but is the noun 'rubbish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is showy sparkle, superficial attractiveness.

clue.text: Joint top-of-the-bill died in the Big Apple, we hear

parts.note: a co-star shares top billing

explanation.surface: A co-starring lead died in New York, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Apple' looks like New York, but a costard is a large old English apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A costard is a large ribbed English cooking apple.

clue.text: Ellis turned out in fine cotton fabric

indicators.note: Ellis turned out is the name shaken up into another order

explanation.surface: A man named Ellis appeared in smart cotton clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'dressed', but rearranges ELLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Mysteries of the variable south wind?

indicators.note: variable means the letters of south wind change their order

explanation.surface: Puzzles about which way the shifting southerly breeze is blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' looks like a weather term for wind, but rearranges SOUTH WIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective novels are called mysteries, the classic one asking who committed the crime.

clue.text: At what point is ewer broken round head of husband?

indicators.note: round means the broken letters circle the husband's first letter
broken means the ewer is smashed into a new order of letters
head of means the opening letter of husband

explanation.surface: Where did a jug get smashed over a husband's head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns EWER to WERE, which goes 'round' H.
explanation.definitionFit: At what point means in which place, a question word.

clue.text: Drug-addicts employ ends of reefers

parts.note: to employ is to use

indicators.note: ends of means the first and last letters of reefers

explanation.surface: Junkies smoke the ends of joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reefers' are cannabis cigarettes, but give only R and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug users are people who take drugs.

clue.text: Carriage is right in the soup

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the soup

parts.note: potage is a thick French soup

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn coach is properly in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for 'in trouble', but 'in' puts R inside POTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the carrying of boats or goods overland, and also the charge for that carrying.

clue.text: Complex sort, this daughter of Agamemnon

explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is a Freudian term for a girl's attachment to her father, and in Greek myth she was Agamemnon's child.

clue.text: Umpire about to call-late?

parts.note: over is the umpire's call at the end of six balls in cricket
due to means about to, expected to happen

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire is about to make a call, behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the umpire calls 'over' after each set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed its expected time, so it is late.

clue.text: Poised like a policy-holder

explanation.definitionFit: Poised means self-confident, and someone holding a life policy is insured.
